title: Protocol for vision transformer-based evaluation of drug potency using images processed by an optimized Sobel operator
protocol: Take a vial of cancer cells from the liquid nitrogen tank.
Thaw the vial in a water bath at 37°C.
Centrifuge the vial at 800 g for 4 minutes.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 10 mL of DMEM complete culture medium.
Culture the cells in a T75 flask in an incubator at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 24 hours.
Remove the culture medium from the flask after 24 hours.
Rinse the flask with 3 mL PBS.
Digest the cells with TrypLe Select enzyme.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 800 g for 4 minutes.
Resuspend and count the cells.
Choose a plate based on the number of drugs to be tested (e.g., 96-well, 384-well, or 1536-well plates).
Seed the cells at a concentration of 6,000 cells per well for 96-well plates.
Prepare stock solutions by dissolving drugs in DMSO.
Dilute the stock solutions with DMEM complete culture medium and prepare the first concentration for the drug (e.g., 200 μM Cephalotaxine and Fasudil).
Prepare a serial dilution by mixing 1 volume of the previous solution with 2 volumes of the DMEM complete culture medium, i.e., 1:3 dilution.
Remove the old media and replace them with 200 μL solution containing drugs and fresh culture media.
Keep the microplates in the incubator at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 24 h.
Turn on the ImageXpress Pico imaging system.
Double-click CRX App (CRX-2.6.130 for Windows 10) to open the application.
Click “ACQUISITION” on the home page.
Click “ADD PROTOCOL.”
Select “96 Corning 3603.”
Turn off all “STAINS.”
Set “TL” to “Capture first.”
Select 4× objective.
Choose 29.8% setting.
Select the wells of interest.
Fill in the protocol name and save the protocol.
Fill in the experiment name and start imaging.
Return to the home page and click “MONITOR” to check the status of the experiment.
Define the vertical filter as [[-1,-2,-1], [0,0,0], [1,2,1]].
Define the horizontal filter as [[-1,0,1], [-2,0,2], [-1,0,1]].
Initialize file_count to 0.
For each image in png_dir:
Read the image using mpimg.imread.
Determine the number of pixels in rows (n) and columns (m).
Initialize edges_img as an array of zeros with the same dimensions as img.
For each pixel row from 3 to n-2:
For each pixel column from 3 to m-2:
Extract local_pixels from img centered at current row and column.
Calculate vertical_transformed_pixels by multiplying vertical_filter with local_pixels.
Sum vertical_transformed_pixels to get vertical_score.
Calculate horizontal_transformed_pixels by multiplying horizontal_filter with local_pixels.
Sum horizontal_transformed_pixels to get horizontal_score.
Compute edge_score using the square root of (vertical_score squared + horizontal_score squared).
If edge_score is greater than or equal to 0.2, adjust edge_score by raising it to the power of 0.6.
Raise edge_score to the power of 0.8 and assign it to edges_img at current row and column.
Save edges_img using plt.imsave with a gray color map in EDGE_PNG_SAVE_DIR followed by "_edge_" + png_files[file_count].
Increment file_count by 1.
Print "Done" after processing all images.
Split each image into 100 patches using PhotoScape X.
Open the file under “Viewer” in PhotoScape X.
Right-click the image and select “Split.”
Change the numbers of “Columns” and “Rows” to specify 10 columns and 10 rows.
Click “Split” to generate sub-images.
Train a Conv2D model.
Randomly split data into training and testing sets using Python scripts for reproducibility.
Assign files into corresponding subfolders based on the split.
Load the test set and rescale the data.
Resize the images in the test set to 201x201 pixels.
Choose "binary classification" for the test set.
Set the batch size for testing to 10.
Resize the images in the validation set to 201x201 pixels.
Choose "binary classification" for the validation set.
Set the batch size for validation to 10.
Train a Conv2D model using the specified architecture.
Add a Conv2D layer with 64 filters, kernel size of (3,3), and ReLU activation.
Connect an input shape of (196, 196, 3) to the first layer.
Add a MaxPooling2D layer with pool size of (2,2).
Add another Conv2D layer with 64 filters, kernel size of (3,3), and ReLU activation.
Add another MaxPooling2D layer with pool size of (2,2).
Add a third Conv2D layer with 128 filters, kernel size of (3,3), and ReLU activation.
Add a third MaxPooling2D layer with pool size of (2,2).
Add a fourth Conv2D layer with 128 filters, kernel size of (3,3), and ReLU activation.
Add a fourth MaxPooling2D layer with pool size of (2,2).
Flatten the results to feed into a DNN.
Add a dropout layer with rate of 0.5.
Add a dense layer with 512 neurons and ReLU activation.
Add an output layer with 1 neuron and sigmoid activation.
Compile the model using binary crossentropy loss function.
Set the optimizer for the model compilation.
Launch Jupyter Notebook from Anaconda and open the file "Vision_Transformer_code.ipynb".
Import packages.
Load the images.
Choose binary classification and specify batch sizes.
Set training parameters.
Data augmentation.
Define multilayer perceptron and patches.
Train the transformer model.
Create a multi-head attention layer.
Evaluate the model using the test set.
Open the file in ImageJ.
Modify the image by subtracting background noise.
Set parameters for "Analyze Particles" tool.
Select “Process > Subtract Background” and adjust parameters.
Click “OK” to apply settings.
Select “Image > Adjust > Threshold”, adjust parameters.
Select "Graph Type" in the popup window and click "OK".
Double-click the X-axis on the graph.
Select “Log 10” for “Scale”.
Select “Short” for “Ticks length”.
Select “Power of 10” for “Format”.
Click “OK”.
Click “Analyze”.
Select “Nonlinear regression (curve fit)” under “XY analyses”.
Click “OK”.

Click “OK”.
Check the IC50 value.
